headline: Two IDE assistants overlap on buffers — moderate prompt injection via shared workspace; little execution conflict because Continue does not run shell.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Both ingest buffer content and the workspace. A suggestion accepted in one is later read by the other. Continue without local models also calls vendor APIs; outputs can entrench attacker-controlled strings if either reads code containing them.
mitigations: Pick one assistant per file; do not have both auto-edit the same buffer

B_data_leakage.rationale: Continue can run fully local with Ollama, eliminating its leak path; Cursor sends to its proxy unless Privacy Mode is on. With both online, two vendors see the same code.
mitigations: Run Continue with a local model via Ollama

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Continue does not execute shell or commit; conflict is bounded to overlapping buffer edits which the IDE serializes.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Each may build on the other's accepted suggestion without verification — but both are edit-time, so user review is in the loop more than with autonomous agents.

E_compliance.rationale: Continue is fully under user control (especially with local models); Cursor has its own data terms. Easy to align.
